validated_results.title: A prospective study of diet and prostate cancer in Japanese men.
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort of Japanese men assessing dietary intake including soya products and incident prostate cancer, with a reported null association for soya products.

extraction.timing: Pre-diagnosis dietary assessment at baseline with follow-up for incident cases
extraction.population: Men in the Life Span Study cohort in Hiroshima and Nagasaki

sample_size.excerpt: This study aimed to examine the association between dietary intake and prostate cancer risk among 18,115 men in Hiroshima and Nagasaki, Japan, using prospective data from the Life Span Study. Subjects completed a food-frequency questionnaire at baseline (1963, 1965 and/or 1979) and were followed for incident prostate cancer until the end of 1996.

cases.excerpt: During this time, 196 incident prostate cancer cases were identified after 252,602 person-years of observation.

comparison.excerpt: No other food items, including soya products, were significantly associated with prostate cancer risk.

design.excerpt: using prospective data from the Life Span Study
